summary.text: Setting up OAuth for Notion involves creating a public connection in the Developer portal, configuring OAuth details, and following a standard OAuth 2.0 flow, but developers may encounter 'invalid_client' errors when logging in or updating.
summary.label: sourced

sources.quote: Navigate to the Developer portal and create a new public connection. Fill out the form with your connection details, including your redirect URI(s) under the OAuth configuration section and the connection’s installation scope — either Any workspace or Selected workspaces only. This can’t be changed after creation.

effort.text: To make a first test call, you can use the Quickstart to create a personal access token and make your first API request.
effort.label: uncertain

sources.quote: The fastest way to start building is the Quickstart — create a personal access token, make your first API request, and see a new page appear in your workspace in under two minutes.

wait.text: You can see a new page appear in your workspace in under two minutes after starting the Quickstart.
wait.label: uncertain

sources.quote: The fastest way to start building is the Quickstart — create a personal access token, make your first API request, and see a new page appear in your workspace in under two minutes.

effort.text: To go to production, you must create a public connection in the Developer portal, implement the OAuth 2.0 flow, and submit the connection for Notion security review if you want it listed on the Marketplace.
effort.label: uncertain

sources.quote: Public connections must undergo a Notion security review before being listed on the Marketplace. You can create and use a public connection without listing it.
